# Setup

```{r}
#| message: false
#| warning: false

library(tidyverse)
library(lubridate)
library(tidymodels)
library(baguette)
library(ranger)
library(rpart.plot)
library(vip)

tidymodels_prefer()

set.seed(558)
```

# Reading the Data

For Homework 10, we continue using the Seoul Bike Sharing dataset from Homework 9.

```{r}
bike_raw <- readr::read_csv(
  "https://www4.stat.ncsu.edu/~online/datasets/SeoulBikeData.csv",
  locale = locale(encoding = "ISO-8859-1"),
  show_col_types = FALSE
)
```

# Cleaning the Data

We convert the date into an R date object and convert the categorical variables into factors.

```{r}
bike <- bike_raw |>
  mutate(
    Date = dmy(Date),
    Seasons = factor(Seasons),
    Holiday = factor(Holiday),
    `Functioning Day` = factor(`Functioning Day`)
  )
```

We also rename the variables so that they are easier to use.

```{r}
bike <- bike |>
  rename(
    date = Date,
    bike_count = `Rented Bike Count`,
    hour = Hour,
    temp = `Temperature(°C)`,
    humidity = `Humidity(%)`,
    wind_speed = `Wind speed (m/s)`,
    visibility = `Visibility (10m)`,
    dew_point_temp = `Dew point temperature(°C)`,
    solar_radiation = `Solar Radiation (MJ/m2)`,
    rainfall = `Rainfall(mm)`,
    snowfall = `Snowfall (cm)`,
    seasons = Seasons,
    holiday = Holiday,
    functioning_day = `Functioning Day`
  )
```

```{r}
glimpse(bike)
```

# Initial Summaries

## Rentals by Season

```{r}
bike |>
  group_by(seasons) |>
  summarise(
    count = n(),
    mean_bikes = mean(bike_count),
    median_bikes = median(bike_count),
    sd_bikes = sd(bike_count),
    .groups = "drop"
  )
```

## Rentals by Holiday

```{r}
bike |>
  group_by(holiday) |>
  summarise(
    count = n(),
    mean_bikes = mean(bike_count),
    median_bikes = median(bike_count),
    sd_bikes = sd(bike_count),
    .groups = "drop"
  )
```

## Rentals by Functioning Day

```{r}
bike |>
  group_by(functioning_day) |>
  summarise(
    count = n(),
    total_bikes = sum(bike_count),
    mean_bikes = mean(bike_count),
    .groups = "drop"
  )
```

The non-functioning days do not contain meaningful bike rental activity, so we restrict the analysis to functioning days.

```{r}
bike <- bike |>
  filter(functioning_day == "Yes")
```

# Create Daily Data

The original dataset contains hourly observations. As in Homework 9, we summarize the dataset so that each day has one observation.

```{r}
daily <- bike |>
  group_by(
    date,
    seasons,
    holiday
  ) |>
  summarise(
    bike_count = sum(bike_count, na.rm = TRUE),
    rainfall = sum(rainfall, na.rm = TRUE),
    snowfall = sum(snowfall, na.rm = TRUE),
    temp = mean(temp, na.rm = TRUE),
    humidity = mean(humidity, na.rm = TRUE),
    wind_speed = mean(wind_speed, na.rm = TRUE),
    visibility = mean(visibility, na.rm = TRUE),
    dew_point_temp = mean(dew_point_temp, na.rm = TRUE),
    solar_radiation = mean(solar_radiation, na.rm = TRUE),
    .groups = "drop"
  )
```

```{r}
dim(daily)
glimpse(daily)
summary(daily)
```

# Training and Test Split

We use the `tidymodels` framework to create a 75/25 training/test split. The split is stratified by season.

```{r}
set.seed(558)

bike_split <- initial_split(
  daily,
  prop = 0.75,
  strata = seasons
)

bike_train <- training(
  bike_split
)

bike_test <- testing(
  bike_split
)
```

```{r}
nrow(bike_train)
nrow(bike_test)
```

# 10-Fold Cross-Validation

We create ten cross-validation folds using only the training data.

```{r}
set.seed(558)

bike_folds <- vfold_cv(
  bike_train,
  v = 10,
  strata = seasons
)

bike_folds
```

# Modeling Metrics

We will compare models using RMSE and MAE.

```{r}
reg_metrics <- metric_set(
  rmse,
  mae
)
```

# Recipe 1

The first recipe:

- creates a weekday/weekend variable from the date,
- removes the original date,
- standardizes the numeric predictors,
- and creates dummy variables for categorical predictors.

```{r}
recipe1 <- recipe(
  bike_count ~ .,
  data = bike_train
) |>
  step_date(
    date,
    features = "dow"
  ) |>
  step_mutate(
    day_type = factor(
      if_else(
        date_dow %in% c("Sat", "Sun"),
        "Weekend",
        "Weekday"
      )
    )
  ) |>
  step_rm(
    date,
    date_dow
  ) |>
  step_normalize(
    all_numeric_predictors()
  ) |>
  step_dummy(
    all_nominal_predictors()
  )
```

```{r}
recipe1
```

# Recipe 2

Recipe 2 contains the same preprocessing steps as Recipe 1 and additionally includes:

- season × holiday interactions,
- season × temperature interactions,
- temperature × rainfall interaction.

```{r}
recipe2 <- recipe(
  bike_count ~ .,
  data = bike_train
) |>
  step_date(
    date,
    features = "dow"
  ) |>
  step_mutate(
    day_type = factor(
      if_else(
        date_dow %in% c("Sat", "Sun"),
        "Weekend",
        "Weekday"
      )
    )
  ) |>
  step_rm(
    date,
    date_dow
  ) |>
  step_normalize(
    all_numeric_predictors()
  ) |>
  step_dummy(
    all_nominal_predictors()
  ) |>
  step_interact(
    terms =
      ~ starts_with("seasons_"):
        starts_with("holiday_") +
        starts_with("seasons_"):temp +
        temp:rainfall
  )
```

```{r}
recipe2
```

# Recipe 3

Recipe 3 contains everything in Recipe 2 and adds quadratic terms for standardized temperature and humidity.

```{r}
recipe3 <- recipe(
  bike_count ~ .,
  data = bike_train
) |>
  step_date(
    date,
    features = "dow"
  ) |>
  step_mutate(
    day_type = factor(
      if_else(
        date_dow %in% c("Sat", "Sun"),
        "Weekend",
        "Weekday"
      )
    )
  ) |>
  step_rm(
    date,
    date_dow
  ) |>
  step_normalize(
    all_numeric_predictors()
  ) |>
  step_dummy(
    all_nominal_predictors()
  ) |>
  step_interact(
    terms =
      ~ starts_with("seasons_"):
        starts_with("holiday_") +
        starts_with("seasons_"):temp +
        temp:rainfall
  ) |>
  step_mutate(
    temp_squared = temp^2,
    humidity_squared = humidity^2
  )
```

```{r}
recipe3
```

# Multiple Linear Regression Specification

All three MLR models use the standard `lm` engine.

```{r}
lm_spec <- linear_reg() |>
  set_engine("lm")
```

# MLR Workflow 1

```{r}
lm_wf1 <- workflow() |>
  add_recipe(recipe1) |>
  add_model(lm_spec)
```

# MLR Workflow 2

```{r}
lm_wf2 <- workflow() |>
  add_recipe(recipe2) |>
  add_model(lm_spec)
```

# MLR Workflow 3

```{r}
lm_wf3 <- workflow() |>
  add_recipe(recipe3) |>
  add_model(lm_spec)
```

# Cross-Validation for the MLR Models

## Model 1

```{r}
set.seed(558)

lm_res1 <- fit_resamples(
  lm_wf1,
  resamples = bike_folds,
  metrics = reg_metrics
)

collect_metrics(lm_res1)
```

## Model 2

```{r}
set.seed(558)

lm_res2 <- fit_resamples(
  lm_wf2,
  resamples = bike_folds,
  metrics = reg_metrics
)

collect_metrics(lm_res2)
```

## Model 3

```{r}
set.seed(558)

lm_res3 <- fit_resamples(
  lm_wf3,
  resamples = bike_folds,
  metrics = reg_metrics
)

collect_metrics(lm_res3)
```

# Compare MLR Cross-Validation Error

```{r}
mlr_cv_results <- bind_rows(
  collect_metrics(lm_res1) |>
    mutate(model = "MLR 1"),
  collect_metrics(lm_res2) |>
    mutate(model = "MLR 2"),
  collect_metrics(lm_res3) |>
    mutate(model = "MLR 3")
) |>
  filter(.metric == "rmse") |>
  select(
    model,
    mean,
    std_err
  ) |>
  arrange(mean)

mlr_cv_results
```

The model with the smallest cross-validation RMSE is selected as the best MLR.

```{r}
best_mlr_name <- mlr_cv_results$model[1]

best_mlr_name
```

```{r}
best_mlr_workflow <- switch(
  best_mlr_name,
  "MLR 1" = lm_wf1,
  "MLR 2" = lm_wf2,
  "MLR 3" = lm_wf3
)
```

# Final MLR Fit

The selected MLR workflow is fit using the entire training set and evaluated on the test set using `last_fit()`.

```{r}
set.seed(558)

mlr_last <- last_fit(
  best_mlr_workflow,
  split = bike_split,
  metrics = reg_metrics
)

collect_metrics(mlr_last)
```

# Regression Tree

We now use Recipe 1 to fit a tuned regression tree.

```{r}
tree_spec <- decision_tree(
  cost_complexity = tune(),
  tree_depth = tune(),
  min_n = tune()
) |>
  set_engine("rpart") |>
  set_mode("regression")
```

```{r}
tree_wf <- workflow() |>
  add_recipe(recipe1) |>
  add_model(tree_spec)
```

## Tune Regression Tree

```{r}
set.seed(558)

tree_grid <- grid_regular(
  cost_complexity(),
  tree_depth(),
  min_n(),
  levels = 4
)

tree_grid
```

```{r}
set.seed(558)

tree_tune <- tune_grid(
  tree_wf,
  resamples = bike_folds,
  grid = tree_grid,
  metrics = reg_metrics
)
```

```{r}
collect_metrics(tree_tune) |>
  filter(.metric == "rmse") |>
  arrange(mean)
```

```{r}
best_tree <- select_best(
  tree_tune,
  metric = "rmse"
)

best_tree
```

```{r}
final_tree_wf <- finalize_workflow(
  tree_wf,
  best_tree
)
```

## Final Regression Tree

```{r}
tree_last <- last_fit(
  final_tree_wf,
  split = bike_split,
  metrics = reg_metrics
)

collect_metrics(tree_last)
```

# Bagged Tree

Next we fit a tuned bagged regression tree using Recipe 1.

```{r}
bag_spec <- bag_tree(
  cost_complexity = tune(),
  min_n = tune()
) |>
  set_engine(
    "rpart",
    times = 25,
    control = control_bag(
      var_imp = TRUE
    )
  ) |>
  set_mode("regression")
```

```{r}
bag_wf <- workflow() |>
  add_recipe(recipe1) |>
  add_model(bag_spec)
```

## Tune Bagged Tree

```{r}
set.seed(558)

bag_grid <- grid_regular(
  cost_complexity(),
  min_n(),
  levels = 4
)

bag_grid
```

```{r}
set.seed(558)

bag_tune <- tune_grid(
  bag_wf,
  resamples = bike_folds,
  grid = bag_grid,
  metrics = reg_metrics
)
```

```{r}
collect_metrics(bag_tune) |>
  filter(.metric == "rmse") |>
  arrange(mean)
```

```{r}
best_bag <- select_best(
  bag_tune,
  metric = "rmse"
)

best_bag
```

```{r}
final_bag_wf <- finalize_workflow(
  bag_wf,
  best_bag
)
```

## Final Bagged Tree

```{r}
bag_last <- last_fit(
  final_bag_wf,
  split = bike_split,
  metrics = reg_metrics
)

collect_metrics(bag_last)
```

# Random Forest

The last model family is a tuned random forest.

```{r}
rf_spec <- rand_forest(
  mtry = tune(),
  min_n = tune(),
  trees = 500
) |>
  set_engine(
    "ranger",
    importance = "impurity"
  ) |>
  set_mode("regression")
```

```{r}
rf_wf <- workflow() |>
  add_recipe(recipe1) |>
  add_model(rf_spec)
```

## Tune Random Forest

Because `mtry` depends on the number of predictors after preprocessing, we use a Latin hypercube grid.

```{r}
rf_params <- extract_parameter_set_dials(
  rf_wf
) |>
  update(
    mtry = mtry(
      c(1L, 15L)
    )
  )
```

```{r}
set.seed(558)

rf_grid <- grid_latin_hypercube(
  rf_params,
  size = 20
)

rf_grid
```

```{r}
set.seed(558)

rf_tune <- tune_grid(
  rf_wf,
  resamples = bike_folds,
  grid = rf_grid,
  metrics = reg_metrics
)
```

```{r}
collect_metrics(rf_tune) |>
  filter(.metric == "rmse") |>
  arrange(mean)
```

```{r}
best_rf <- select_best(
  rf_tune,
  metric = "rmse"
)

best_rf
```

```{r}
final_rf_wf <- finalize_workflow(
  rf_wf,
  best_rf
)
```

## Final Random Forest

```{r}
rf_last <- last_fit(
  final_rf_wf,
  split = bike_split,
  metrics = reg_metrics
)

collect_metrics(rf_last)
```

# Compare All Models on the Test Set

We compare the final MLR, regression tree, bagged tree, and random forest using both RMSE and MAE.

```{r}
test_results <- bind_rows(
  collect_metrics(mlr_last) |>
    mutate(model = "MLR"),
  collect_metrics(tree_last) |>
    mutate(model = "Regression Tree"),
  collect_metrics(bag_last) |>
    mutate(model = "Bagged Tree"),
  collect_metrics(rf_last) |>
    mutate(model = "Random Forest")
) |>
  select(
    model,
    .metric,
    .estimate
  )

test_results
```

## RMSE Comparison

```{r}
test_results |>
  filter(.metric == "rmse") |>
  arrange(.estimate)
```

## MAE Comparison

```{r}
test_results |>
  filter(.metric == "mae") |>
  arrange(.estimate)
```

# Overall Best Test Model

We choose the model with the smallest test RMSE.

```{r}
best_overall <- test_results |>
  filter(.metric == "rmse") |>
  arrange(.estimate) |>
  slice(1)

best_overall
```

# Fit the Overall Best Model to the Entire Dataset

The homework asks us to take the overall best model and fit it using all available observations.

```

  "Regression Tree" = final_tree_wf,

```

# Conclusion

For this analysis, we used the `tidymodels` framework to compare several approaches for predicting daily bike rental counts.

Three multiple linear regression models were first compared using 10-fold cross-validation. We then tuned a regression tree, bagged tree, and random forest using the same training-set resamples.

The best model from each family was fit using the complete training data and evaluated on the held-out test data using both RMSE and MAE.

The model with the smallest test RMSE was then selected as the overall best model and refit using the complete dataset.
